correctness.rationale: For m≥2 pairwise mutually singular positive probabilities on perfect compact metric K, the functionals are linearly independent and every projection onto their common kernel has f↦f−Σ_j μ_j(f)g_j with μ_i(g_j)=δ_ij. Mutual singularity and the Daugavet finite-rank identity yield ||P||=1+max_xΣ_j|g_j(x)|. Continuous almost-disjoint support cutoffs give infimum 2; equality forces g_j=1 on supp μ_j, each g_i=0 on all other supports, so the closed supports must be pairwise disjoint; continuous separation proves the converse. The weak-topology dense Gδ of pairwise singular, diffuse, full-support probabilities forces generic nonattainment; finite distinct-atom tuples force density of attainment, hence a dense meagre attainment stratum. For μ_1=dx,μ_2=δ_0, integrating Re g_1≤min(Lx,1+ε) yields L≥(1+ε)^2/(2ε); the displayed tent-function g_1,g_2 give ||P_t||=2+2/(2t−1), Lip=t+t/(2t−1), verifying optimal inverse-error order but not its leading constant. The source CHECK.py contains finite rational corroboration, not an infinite proof.
